bestiary.block.csrp.biomass_block.desc: Hurts anything that touches it. It constantly seeps green vapors and dripping biomass. Parasites aren't harmed by it.
bestiary.block.csrp.biomepurifier.desc: Purifies the beckon Infestation if left alone and there are no Beckons nearby. Interacting with Purifier removes parasite biomes LOGICALLY once node has been cleared.
bestiary.block.csrp.diseased_sponge.desc: Can be brewed with water bottles or Awkward Potions to create §2Dead Blood Fluid§7.
bestiary.block.csrp.esca_bulb.desc: Smells and Feels like Rotting fish. Packed with Bioluminescence.
bestiary.block.csrp.fog_nullifier.desc: Destroys connected Fog Blocks. Breaks after the third use. Cannot be picked up.

bestiary.block.csrp.infested_remain.desc: Can be removed using fire. Used in crafting and harvesting of Residue Bloomings.

bestiary.block.csrp.node_redstone_lamp.d: A fragile glass node wired into Dispatchers within a 250-block range. bestiary.block.csrp.parasite_barrier.des: Pushes all SRParasites entities outwards. Can be cycled through a 1 - 10 chunk radius.

bestiary.block.csrp.parasitemouth.desc: A fleshy parasite mouth embedded in the ground. Anything that steps directly on it gets bitten, taking armor-piercing damage and gaining corrosive and viral infections. Parasites and players in Creative mode are unaffected.

bestiary.block.csrp.sick_alveoli.desc: A weakened, infected form of the Alveoli Block. It poisons any creature that touches it and will remain diseased until brought close to a Bronchial Tube.

bestiary.effect.adapted.desc: Damage dealt to adapted parasite variants is reduced while this effect is active.
bestiary.effect.antimall.desc: Reduces or removes adaptive resistance in malleable parasites.
bestiary.effect.bleed.desc: The host suffers continuous internal bleeding. Damage scales with maximum health and worsens while moving.
bestiary.effect.braining.desc: Disrupts perception of parasites. While active, parasite entities will not render on the client (they still exist and act normally), updated once per-second.
bestiary.effect.conta.desc: The host is biologically contaminated, suffering periodic damage and risking spread to nearby entities.
bestiary.effect.corrosive.desc: Corrosive substances eat away at the host, dealing periodic damage over time.
bestiary.effect.coth.desc: An assimilative infection that escalates in stages. It can refresh and intensify, spread to nearby living hosts (unless repelled), and eventually trigger conversion when the host is weakened or progression thresholds are met.
bestiary.effect.crude.desc: Damage dealt to crude parasite variants is reduced while this effect is active.
bestiary.effect.debar.desc: Suppresses parasite loot. Parasites affected by Debar will not generate their configured drops on death (respecting the doMobLoot gamerule).
The mind is forced to bear witness to a truth it was never built to survive, leaving the body shining like a marked target before entities that should not notice it. While active, the afflicted glows, takes 5x damage from the Draconite, takes 20%% less damage from other parasites, and deals 20%% less damage to parasites. Sentient weapons can deflect projectiles that apply this effect.
bestiary.effect.dod_smoke_trail.desc: A constant trail of thick smoke follows the afflicted entity.
bestiary.effect.effectneg.desc: Intensifies harmful effects. While active, negative potion effects on the host are strengthened, scaling with effect strength.
bestiary.effect.effectpos.desc: Punishes beneficial effects. The host suffers damage based on the number of active positive potion effects, scaling with effect strength.
bestiary.effect.fear.desc: A crippling panic response that disrupts control. At higher levels it can randomly prevent using items or interacting with blocks, cancelling item use outright (subject to blacklist/whitelist rules). Fear also amplifies fall damage and can increase damage taken while airborne, scaling with effect strength and configuration.
bestiary.effect.feral.desc: Damage dealt to feral parasite variants is reduced while this effect is active.
bestiary.effect.foster.desc: The host is marked as suitable for parasitic growth, drawing the attention and protection of nearby parasites.
bestiary.effect.indeaf.desc: Severs movement control. While active, movement inputs (forward/back/jump) are forcibly disabled and horizontal motion is continually cancelled, effectively rooting the host in place.
bestiary.effect.jugg.desc: A dislodgement-bound effect that triggers on death. Depending on active Dislo codes, nearby parasites may be healed, nearby non-parasites may be damaged, and nearby players may suffer exhaustion. Certain deaths also apply a Jugg surge to the killer for a short time, with strength tied to stored dislocation values.
bestiary.effect.link.desc: Links the host to a colony network. While active, colony-related reactions (such as adaptation/colony triggers) become more likely, scaling with effect strength. Some colony entities can also propagate Link to nearby parasites, synchronizing them as part of the colony.
bestiary.effect.muscleout.desc: Greatly increases the host's outgoing damage. Attacks are multiplied by a configuration-based factor that scales with effect strength (amplifier + 1).
bestiary.effect.needler.desc: Parasitic growths erupt from the host, launching needle-like projectiles that damage nearby entities.
bestiary.effect.nexus.desc: Damage dealt to nexus-linked parasite entities is reduced while this effect is active.
bestiary.effect.novision.desc: The host's vision is smothered by a full-screen impairment and mining fatigue is applied; commonly inflicted while a parasite is latched onto host.
bestiary.effect.overheating.desc: The host's body overheats, suffering escalating damage as internal systems begin to fail.
bestiary.effect.parate.desc: A mutative surge that boosts core combat stats. While active, the host's maximum health, armor, and attack damage are increased by a percentage of their base values (scaled by effect strength and configuration multiplier).
bestiary.effect.pivot.desc: While active, kills contribute increased evolution/progression points (scaled by a multiplier and effect strength), and certain parasite events may treat pivot-marked entities as a stronger "signal" when evaluating spawns or stages.
bestiary.effect.prey.desc: The host is designated as prey, making them more likely to be hunted and targeted by parasites.
bestiary.effect.primitive.desc: Damage dealt to primitive parasite variants is reduced while this effect is active.
bestiary.effect.pure.desc: Damage dealt to pure parasite variants is reduced while this effect is active.
bestiary.effect.rage.desc: The host enters a violent frenzy, increasing movement speed and attack damage. Both bonuses can be multiplied and scale with effect strength (values are configuration-based).
bestiary.effect.repel.desc: A repellent mark that protects the host from Call of the Hive infection. While active, it can block assimilation-related behaviors such as conversion/transform triggers and helps prevent nearby spread.
bestiary.effect.senses.desc: The host's sensory perception is heightened, increasing detection and follow range.
bestiary.effect.spotted.desc: The host has been marked and is easier for parasites to track and locate.
bestiary.effect.the_sign.desc: The host bears a mark of significance. Parasites will ignore their presence while the sign persists. The Sign is a bright red symbol possessed by only a select number of people. Among these individuals, the Sign is considered to be a signifier of traits such as great potential, specialness, and competent leadership. The Sign grants immunity to Derived Distortion Phenomenon and parasite aggression.
bestiary.effect.thornshade_thorns.desc: Barbed growths erupt from the host, damaging those who physically strike them. The host will violently erupt if afflicted with said-affect more than 2 times. Nearby entities afflicted with same affects and will erupt if too close to the host during eruption. Does not break tiles.
bestiary.effect.viral.desc: A rapidly mutating infection spreads through the host, dealing periodic damage and risking transmission to nearby living entities. Higher effect levels increase severity and spread potential.

bestiary.progress.term.assimilated.toolt: Assimilated Mobs are the Assimilated variants of vanilla mobs, which have been overtaken by the infection through Call Of The Hive.
bestiary.progress.term.beckons.tooltip: Infection structures that grow into stronger stages as the world progresses.
bestiary.progress.term.buglins.tooltip: Small grub-like parasites that appear during the earliest phase. They spawn in groups of 2 to 6. They can emerge from Tunnel blocks.
bestiary.progress.term.collective_consci: Parasites begin sharing awareness through a wider connected network.
bestiary.progress.term.colonies.tooltip: Large parasite colony structures can be constructed.
bestiary.progress.term.coth.tooltip: Call of the Hive. Infected mobs can mutate or hide parasite behavior.
bestiary.progress.term.crop_growth.toolt: At higher phases, crop growth is partially slowed or disrupted.
bestiary.progress.term.dislodgment.toolt: Applies certain buffs to Parasites and debuffs on non-Parasites, all based on RNG, and the player's actions. In turn for the benefits, each event consumes a set amount of Evolution Points and set a cooldown to the code that was activated. Not all codes will be available in all phases. It is unlocked at Ubiquitous Development Level I. Use the Dislodgment module to check for any current Dislodgment events/codes.
bestiary.progress.term.feral.tooltip: A stronger fodder parasite category that begins appearing naturally at this phase.
bestiary.progress.term.fishing.tooltip: At this phase, fishing is disabled or disrupted by parasite progression.
bestiary.progress.term.merge.tooltip: Assimilated mobs can combine or escalate through merging behavior.
bestiary.progress.term.nests.tooltip: Dispatcher and Rooter structures can begin appearing.
bestiary.progress.term.nodes.tooltip: Node infection structures can spread through the world.
bestiary.progress.term.passive_points.to: Parasite's killcount will go up by 0.05 each second.
bestiary.progress.term.reinforcement.too: A System that allows Beckons (and thus also Nodes and certain Parasites) to appear in the world. It becomes more significant with each passing Phase after initial unlock. After any Parasite larger than one block dies, there's a chance that a Stage I Beckon will emerge from underground, near the given Parasite's death location.
bestiary.progress.term.rupters.tooltip: Fast parasites that begin with benign behavior before becoming more direct attackers.
bestiary.progress.term.scent.tooltip: Parasites can use scent-based tracking systems.
bestiary.progress.term.ubiquitous_mob_ch: Chance for the system to use the Ubiquitous Development mob list instead of the normal evolution-phase mob list.
bestiary.progress.term.vectorless.toolti: Parasites are no longer limited to spawning from infected vectors.

bestiary.system.collective_consciousness: Parasites can act as a single coordinated organism. With Collective Consciousness active, nearby entities share awareness and respond together.
bestiary.system.colonies.desc: Colonies are established 'industrial' segments of the infection. They strengthen parasite presence in an area and make infestations harder to remove. Sponges can be used to remove Dead Blood from Colony structures.
bestiary.system.colonies.name: Colonies
bestiary.system.derived_distortion.desc: Derived parasites emit a disruptive phenomenon that interferes with nearby analysis tools and interfaces. When one is close enough, affected GUI pages may display scrambled text, falsified readouts, and distorted values instead of reliable information. This proximity-based effect causes a black, oily substance to seep from the victim's eyes, while thoughts and senses take on the feeling of a rough, staticky granite surface.
bestiary.system.derived_distortion.name: Derived Distortion Phenomenon
bestiary.system.dislodgment.desc: Certain actions can disturb the infection and provoke retaliation. Dislodgment triggers can activate through interaction, recovery, or parasite activity, escalating responses through multiple tiers of strength. To view the current dislodgment codes and their effects, place a Dislodgment Module in the array and press scan.
bestiary.system.dislodgment.name: Dislodgment
bestiary.system.eiv.desc: When Emerging Infestation Vectors are enabled, parasites can only spawn naturally within the area of an active Vector. These zones can grow over time, and parasites cannot naturally spawn outside of them. If that restriction is disabled in config or SRP world options, parasites are no longer confined to Vector zones and may spawn naturally throughout the world. Each Vector has health points that increase whenever a parasite kills a mob or assimilates one. When either of those happens, the total health of that mob is added to the Vector’s own health. The radius and health of Vectors can also increase independently each day, or roughly every 24000 ticks. To view a Vector's information, place a Vector Module into an Array and press 'Scan'.
bestiary.system.eiv.name: Vectors
bestiary.system.evolution.desc: The infection progresses through evolution phases as it gains strength. Each phase unlocks more behaviors and mechanics. Certain actions, such as using Lure Blocks, can reduce evolution and slow the outbreak's growth.
bestiary.system.evolution.name: Evolution
bestiary.system.generations.desc: Incremental difficulty and tweaks to parasite stats and relating systems. Parasites matures through said-generations over time. Each generation requires sustained growth, and mismatched conditions can slow progress.
bestiary.system.generations.name: Generations
bestiary.system.hives.desc: Hives are structures that organize and defend parasite territory.
bestiary.system.hives.name: Hives
bestiary.system.merge.desc: Assimilated creatures can fuse and reform into new entities. Depending on conditions, merged forms may be selected from specific outcomes or generated randomly.
bestiary.system.merge.name: Merge
bestiary.system.nests.desc: Specialized Relay(Nexus) parasites such as Dispatchers can form nests that accelerate growth and expansion for the hive. These sites rapidly turn surrounding terrain into active and foggy infestation zones. A Fog Nullifier can be used to remove said-fog.
bestiary.system.nests.name: Nests
bestiary.system.nodes.desc: Nodes serve as infrastructure for parasite expansion. When active, they support spreading and reinforce nearby growth.
bestiary.system.nodes.name: Nodes
bestiary.system.reinforcement.desc: When a parasite is killed, it may signal for help. A Beckon can appear nearby and begin summoning allies. Beckons grow through stages, and higher stages bring stronger or more numerous reinforcements, allowing small encounters to escalate rapidly. It is paramount that Beckons are removed before they're able to grow and evolve.
bestiary.system.reinforcement.name: Reinforcements
bestiary.system.scent.desc: The parasite reacts to activity through 'scent' buildup. As scent levels rise, waves of enemies become more frequent and more aggressive. Careless combat or lingering in infested areas can draw increasingly dangerous responses.
bestiary.system.scent.name: Scent
bestiary.system.status_effects.desc: The parasite inflicts unique status effects such as Fear, COTH, Needler, Bleeding, and Camouflage. These effects interfere with combat, movement, and survival, often stacking or intensifying the longer an encounter continues. Be very cautious when these effects are active.
bestiary.system.status_effects.name: Status Effects
bestiary.system.ubiquitous_development.d: As parasites grow further, new systems begin to activate across the world. Higher development levels unlock mechanics such as coordinated behavior, merging, scent waves, structures, and expanded spawning rules.
bestiary.system.variants.desc: Parasites have a chance to spawn from an array of variants that are not limited to inflicting viral, bleeding, or doing more damage to blocks.
bestiary.system.variants.name: Variants
bestiary.system.vectors.desc: Emerging Infestation Vectors are areas where most parasites are allowed to spawn naturally. If vector spawning is enabled, natural parasite spawns are usually limited to the range of an active Vector. Active Vectors can be viewed with the Vector Module. Every 24000 ticks, the first Vector has a 1 in 3 chance to appear. Once at least one Vector exists, additional Vector creation checks have a 1 in 10 chance to succeed.
bestiary.system.vectors.name: Vectors
bestiary.systems.title: Systems

lore.csrp.airscrew: §lEpithet:§r Leer §l|§r §oIts proboscis yields enough strength to lift a van with ease. The sac above its body keeps it hanging like a spoiled calamari, likely filled with a volatile low-density gas produced in excess by its own tissues and held under enough pressure to offset the creature's weight. The mouth beneath gives off concentrated COTH in wet, choking drafts. Prey caught in its webbed projectiles is drawn upward and worked against the hooked underside of its dislocated maw with similar rhythm one might use to strip meat from bone. More than once, I have seen two or more fight over the same catch, pulling with such blind force that the victim came apart between them. Those that survive the feeding do not always remain whole in mind; the turned variants are sometimes discarded afterward and left to tumble to their deaths.
lore.csrp.beckon_si: §lEpithet:§r Venkrol §l|§r §4WIP§o§0 §l|§r Seed structure that calls parasites like moths to a wound.
lore.csrp.beckon_sii: §lEpithet:§r Venkrol §l|§r §4WIP§o§0 §l|§r The call grows louder; the ground learns to answer back.
lore.csrp.beckon_siii: §lEpithet:§r Venkrol §l|§r §4WIP§o§0 §l|§r Beacon and birthing room; the air tastes like copper and is thick like mud.
lore.csrp.beckon_siv: §lEpithet:§r Venkrol §l|§r §4WIP§o§0 §l|§r An address for the hive. Everything nearby is now an entrance, exit, and void.
lore.csrp.bogle: §lEpithet:§r Lencia §l|§r §4WIP§o§0 §l|§r How does it fly? Regardless of that, only  deep blast craters remain.
lore.csrp.bomber_heavy: §lEpithet:§r Jinjo §l|§r §4WIP§o§0 §l|§r A walking verdict when it arrives, the area is rewritten. Where have I seen this before?
lore.csrp.bomber_light: §lEpithet:§r Omboo §l|§r §4WIP§o§0 §l|§r Hollow frame packed with volatile tissue.
lore.csrp.buglin: §lEpithet:§r Lodo §l|§r §oRoughly the size of a basketball, this grub-like mass is formed from unstable flesh that bends and compresses in ways it should not, often appearing moments from rupturing. It carries a sharp metallic stench, and its substance tastes sour and aggressively acidic. Sixteen small hook-like claws, each about an inch long, line its underside and allow it to crawl across terrain or force itself into and out of living prey. It possesses no visible orifices, its body sealed like a malformed catalyst. Despite its flexibility, the Buglin is fragile under extreme pressure, rupturing instantly beneath the weight of an iron golem. Often found emerging from parasite tunnels.
lore.csrp.carrier_colony: §lEpithet:§r Vesta §l|§r §4WIP§o§0 §l|§r A city of mouths and holes travelling on too many legs. It appears to link and coordinate nearby units, and make them adapt faster and together.
lore.csrp.carrier_flying: §lEpithet:§r Buthol §l|§r §oAn airborne infestation vector that hovers over active infestation zones. Three external bulbous growths hang blow the body, each containing a separate chemical component. When agitated, the compounds are forcibly mixed within the bulbs, causing rapid inflation before the body ruptures outward. Upon exposure to open air, the released mixture converts into a highly toxic, gas-like substance. The creature emits an odor similar to industrial chemical waste. Its surface is lined with fine hypodermic pricks and needle-like protrusions that damage nearby matter during detonation. The resulting compound rapidly melts exposed skin. Fire engulfment appears to destabilize and partially defuse the reaction.
lore.csrp.carrier_heavy: §lEpithet:§r Rathol §l|§r §oA heavy carrier designed to spread dense payloads of filth, toxins, and supporting parasites. The body is fully sealed, displaying no visible orifices, and functions primarily as a pressure vessel for stored noxious gas. Specimens may form empty of living mass yet remain filled with volatile chemical mixtures. Within its compartmental structure, several partially digested parasites remain suspended and mobile, swimming through the slurry. Prior to detonation, the organism dissolves its own internal organs and structural barriers, rapidly building internal pressure before rupturing. It reacts strongly to vibrations and emits an odor comparable to spoiled cooked meat sealed in a warm container. Fire engulfment appears to destabilize and partially defuse the reaction.
lore.csrp.carrier_light: §lEpithet:§r Gothol §l|§r §oA nimble carrier adapted for rapid strikes and short-range seeding. Its body is composed of hundreds of small compartments filled with a volatile slurry chemically bound to its vital functions. Internal organs are densely centralized, forming a firm core similar in structure to the center of a blackberry. Despite its instability, the organism is capable of maintaining balance independently and reacts aggressively to vibrations in its surroundings. It emits an odor comparable to spoiled cooked meat sealed in a warm container. Detonation leaves widespread residue. Fire engulfment appears to destabilize and partially defuse the reaction.
lore.csrp.crux: §lEpithet:§r Cruxa §l|§r §oFramework of a brutish, selfless creature still knitting itself together. Its rage deepens with every corpse it leaves behind. I have seen it hurl its own comrades at fleeing prey, with little care for whether the impact kills them. Under immense strain, its body secretes a strange boiling orange substance, and when driven to great speed, steam rises from it as though the whole frame is on the verge of catching fire. I cannot imagine the force required to keep such a body in motion.
lore.csrp.crux_incomplete: §lEpithet:§r Cruxa §l|§r §oAn outline of awkwardly knitted teeth. What remains is little more than a charred, half-formed frame, buying time and flesh until the fuller body forces its way through. It often settles in shallow creeks and streams to cool itself, as though the water hastens the mending of its crude, misshapen, chrysalis-like body.
lore.csrp.dispatcher_si: §lEpithet:§r Dod §l|§r §4WIP§o§0 §l|§r First dispatcher; signals, orders, and others in tidy loops.
lore.csrp.dispatcher_sii: §lEpithet:§r Dod §l|§r §4WIP§o§0 §l|§r Channels widen; traffic of limbs and messages never ceases.
lore.csrp.dispatcher_siii: §lEpithet:§r Dod §l|§r §4WIP§o§0 §l|§r Logistics perfected and reinforcements arrive before you finish bleeding.
lore.csrp.dispatcher_siv: §lEpithet:§r Dod §l|§r §4WIP§o§0 §l|§r The hub and the highway; strike it down or watch a living continent converge.
lore.csrp.dispatcherten: §lEpithet:§r DodT §l|§r §4WIP§o§0 §l|§r A barbed conduit for orders.
lore.csrp.draconite: §lEpithet:§r Heblu §l|§r It is perpetually caked in ash, burning from the inside out. Its chest and stomach function as a toxic hellforge, cycling extreme heat and corrosive byproducts through its body and the surrounding air. The process melts its own flesh as it runs, rupturing weak points and punching holes clean through its frame. Layers of skin continually char, split, and peel away, giving it a pale, ashy-white appearance. Evidence suggests it was formed from something sealed deep within netherrack, only recently forced back into existence. The growth was so violent and rapid that it shed itself faster than its body could stabilize- its head tearing free from the base of its neck during formation, leaving behind a blunt, stump-like structure. The internal combustion of its core sounds as if a freight train is carrying me through the deepest pits of hell. At times, the core buried in its chest vents everything it has failed to burn away, releasing compressed bursts of distorted, radiant matter that bend through the air as if pulled toward living targets.
lore.csrp.dredge: §lEpithet:§r Done §l|§r §oMeasured violence. Beneath an otherworldly executioner's skull, the body closes in deliberate loops, testing ribs, throat, and spine with the calm precision of something that already knows where the human frame and spirit gives first. The tail binds and strangles, starves the body of air, and leaves the victim reeling with a violent loss of coordination long before death. Its victims are left in a state resembling '§4ataxia telangiectasia§o§0', §obut accelerated into something cruelly immediate. The struggle is prolonged with too much care to be accidental. No other parasite of this tier appears so invested in keeping prey conscious through the worst of it. Whether it feeds on the chemicals of panic or on the memories shaken loose by suffering, I cannot yet say.
lore.csrp.fer_bear: §lEpithet:§r Fer §l|§r §4WIP§o§0 §l|§r Unleashes unstoppable fury, rending prey. As if converted bear wasn't enough.
lore.csrp.fer_cow: §lEpithet:§r Fer §l|§r §4WIP§o§0 §l|§r A lumbering vessel of meat and muscle, driven by endless hunger. The one who denies all.
lore.csrp.fer_enderman: §lEpithet:§r Fer §l|§r §4WIP§o§0 §l|§r Stalks silently, warping through space with feral precision. Can ferry larger things and is not deterred by any water at all. Rage eternal.
lore.csrp.fer_horse: §lEpithet:§r Fer §l|§r §4WIP§o§0 §l|§r Gallops with reckless speed, trampling the fallen in its path.
lore.csrp.fer_human: §lEpithet:§r Fer §l|§r §4WIP§o§0 §l|§r Human form stripped of reason and skin.
lore.csrp.fer_pig: §lEpithet:§r Fer §l|§r §4WIP§o§0 §l|§r A grotesque feeder, squealing with hunger.
lore.csrp.fer_wolf: §lEpithet:§r Fer §l|§r §4WIP§o§0 §l|§r Alpha predator; a relentless hunter.
lore.csrp.gnat: §lEpithet:§r Ata §l|§r §oA small parasitic that uses its tentacles as rotating drill-heads to bore into hosts, allowing it to hijack and control both organic and inorganic entities. Individually weak, its appendages are exceptionally sharp and capable of chewing through dense material and resilient prey. A bulbous growth along its back dissolves or violently ruptures once embedded within a host, accelerating internal damage and takeover. It is heavily attracted to the scent of blood, to the point where it can be deliberately used as a distraction. The organism lacks any form of hearing and relies entirely on scent to navigate. Specimens are often coated in a slick, lubricant-like mucus, a residue from being secreted out of vermin.
lore.csrp.grunt: §lEpithet:§r Flog §l|§r §4WIP§o§0 §l|§r Nothing wasted, nothing spared; advances until one of you stops. A "grunt" to the larger ones out there.
lore.csrp.haunter: §lEpithet:§r Pheon §l|§r §4WIP§o§0 §l|§r A presence felt before seen.
lore.csrp.heed: §lEpithet:§r Heed §l|§r §oFive-headed scout borne on an ant-like frame, with a maw set sideways across the face. It does little leading of its own, instead carrying signals forward and stirring the hunt where resistance is found. I have seen it engage in trophallaxis with smaller, needier parasites.
lore.csrp.hi_skeleton: §lEpithet:§r Hi §l|§r §oA frame for something to stand on.
lore.csrp.host: §lEpithet:§r Host §l|§r §oIt is often said that earthquakes foretell doom. Much of it remains buried, with only otherworldly groans and the stirring ground above betraying where the rest has gone. Corpses are rendered down into a strange black, tar-like matter that binds through its frame and keeps the greater body pliant. Each tentacle ends in a hollow opening put to many uses, from mending torn flesh to feeding from the fallen.
lore.csrp.hostii: §lEpithet:§r Hostii §l|§r §oThe herd moves beneath soft and jagged ground as though its body can yield to every sharp crevice in the tainted soil. What was once a buried carrier has swollen into a heavier colony-form, casting out engorged bombs in quick bursts, each one packed with unknown venom and disease. Beneath the noise of its passing, there are often repeated mutterings that suggest some low, collective intelligence, though nothing in them has yet proven understandable.
lore.csrp.incompleteform_medium: §lEpithet:§r Inhoo §l|§r §oHalf-shaped, wholly lethal. The sort of thing one expects to find scraping at the walls of a body, not running loose without one.
lore.csrp.incompleteform_small: §lEpithet:§r Inhoo §l|§r §oSmall frame, fast cuts. Light in the arms and ugly on impact, like catching a sack filled with teeth. Smells abhorrent and is best taken care of quickly.
lore.csrp.kirin: §lEpithet:§r Kirin §l|§r Kirin exists in a constant state of structural failure. Its body is perpetually on the verge of tearing itself apart, which explains its bruised, bloodied exterior and unstable movements. Large cavities line each of its hollow arm structures, acting as vents for excess heat and bursts of cosmic radiation generated internally. These openings along their body act as vents or outlets- without them, the entity would likely detonate. The strain placed on its form causes Kirin to molt daily. Each projection it manifests further destabilizes its body, forcing layers of damaged tissue to be shed and replaced at an alarming rate. The creature shows no signs of self-preservation. It has not yet failed completely. Else I would be dead.
lore.csrp.kyphosis: §lEpithet:§r Tonro §l|§r §4WIP§o§0 §l|§r Hunched mass that coiled sinew uses as a living shield and battering ram.
lore.csrp.lice: §lEpithet:§r Viin §l|§r §oA highly erratic parasitic that uses its tentacles as rotating drill-heads to burrow into hosts, hijacking and controlling both organic and inorganic entities. Its abdomen is grossly inflated and lined with multiple bulbous growths that serve as both fuel and explosive charges, allowing it to force attachment and penetrate resistant targets. Movement is unpredictable to the point of inefficiency, making it difficult to track or swat. The organism is strongly attracted to the scent of sweat and blood and produces a faint humming noise when in close proximity.
lore.csrp.mangler: §lEpithet:§r Nuuh §l|§r §oA close-quarters brute derived from Rupters, grown specifically for larger prey such as cattle, horses, and llamas. It weighs roughly the same as a large dog and is built for endurance and sustained force rather than speed. While bulkier in form, it retains the transmissible capabilities of its predecessors. The metallic scent present in Rupters is significantly stronger, often detectable before visual contact.
lore.csrp.mar_bear: §lEpithet:§r Mar §l|§r §oNothing about its body makes sense. A colony of spiders nests inside.
lore.csrp.mar_cow: §lEpithet:§r Mar §l|§r §oNothing about its body makes sense. Its internal chamber works ceaselessly.
lore.csrp.mar_enderman: §lEpithet:§r Mar §l|§r §oNothing about its body makes sense. Twisted beyond recognition.
lore.csrp.mar_human: §lEpithet:§r Mar §l|§r §oNothing about its body makes sense. Irritatingly disruptive.
lore.csrp.mar_sheep: §lEpithet:§r Mar §l|§r §oNothing about its body makes sense. A tall vigil.
lore.csrp.mar_villager: §lEpithet:§r Mar §l|§r §oNothing about its body makes sense. The face of the oblivion.
lore.csrp.marauder: §lEpithet:§r Esor §l|§r §4WIP§o§0 §l|§r Carver of corridors through living lines; momentum is its favorite weapon.
lore.csrp.monarch: §lEpithet:§r Orch §l|§r §4WIP§o§0 §l|§r Commands lesser forms by impulse alone; the swarm kneels without thought.
lore.csrp.pri_arachnida: §lEpithet:§r Ranrac §l|§r §oCrude eight-legged horror, precursor to greater forms.
lore.csrp.pri_bolster: §lEpithet:§r Bano e'Zetmo §l|§r §oBulky frame, primitive yet resilient.
lore.csrp.pri_burrower: §lEpithet:§r Zaa §l|§r §oInstinctively digs, carving out nests for others.
lore.csrp.pri_devourer: §lEpithet:§r Lum §l|§r §oGuided only by hunger and the scent of blood in water.
lore.csrp.pri_longarms: §lEpithet:§r Shyco §l|§r §oGrasping limbs lunge far, though clumsy compared to later forms.
lore.csrp.pri_manducater: §lEpithet:§r Hull §l|§r §oGrinding jaws that never cease. Stays out of the eyesight.
lore.csrp.pri_summoner: §lEpithet:§r Canra §l|§r §oCalls lesser spawn in erratic bursts. Re-sews what was slain out of leftovers.
lore.csrp.pri_vermin: §lEpithet:§r Iki §l|§r §oIt's a weather balloon. Its contents are even worse.
lore.csrp.pri_yelloweye: §lEpithet:§r Emana §l|§r §oPonytails of sinew and bone. Its caustic bile is anathema to armor.

lore.csrp.rupter: §lEpithet:§r Mudo §l|§r §oRupters operate in packs, using speed and numbers to split formations and harass isolated targets. When alone they are initially docile, though this behavior is subject to rapid change. Their musculature and tendons are folded into a dense, tesseract-like arrangement, while internal organs sprawl through the body like root systems with no clear structure. They weigh roughly the same as a cannonball and are capable of long, fast jumps, as well as climbing sheer surfaces, though they lack the dexterity to hang from ceilings that well. Tendrils twinge outward when agitated, gripping and boring into targets. Rupters frequently tear through cattle and smaller creatures, often killing them unintentionally. Solid matter is dissolved within the stomach and regurgitated back onto or into victims in small indistinguishable traces to efficiently transmit COTH without much retaliation. Their organs can be harvested, dried, and processed into a durable fiber-like material. Limbs may be torn free from the body similar to a spider; it remains unknown whether lost limbs can regenerate.
lore.csrp.seizer: §lEpithet:§r Nak §l|§r §4WIP§o§0 §l|§r Grabs and pins. Struggling makes it angrier.
lore.csrp.sentry: §lEpithet:§r Unvo §l|§r §4WIP§o§0 §l|§r Their projectiles melt through bone and steel alike.
lore.csrp.sim_adventurer: §lEpithet:§r Sim §l|§r §oObserved traveling in loose groups, but once enough gather, they begin to match pace. They still check containers, doorways, and camp-like structures, as if memory survives in fragments. Occasionally, one will stop and stare into familiar spaces for several seconds, as though trying to remember what it once was. They appear to like assimilated dogs. I guess some things never change.
lore.csrp.sim_bear: §lEpithet:§r Sim §l|§r §oIts body has been preserved for force rather than speed. Specimens do not posture or bluff-charge like healthy bears; once agitated, they commit fully. Trees, barricades, and even damaged walls are treated as inconveniences by this thing. I observed one of them chewing the flesh from its own body once, as if to satiate an itch.
lore.csrp.sim_bigspider: §lEpithet:§r Dorpa §l|§r §oThis one produces excessive webbing mixed with foul organic runoff. Trails left behind often remain contaminated long after the host has passed. Its movements are strangely deliberate, as if it is less interested in pursuit and more concerned with spreading material across as much ground as possible. This one has a discernible temper, and I once witnessed it relentlessly stab holes into a pig with its legs, like a horse trampling a mound of flesh. I can only assume it did this because the prey was loud; it did not bother infesting it. Perhaps it was just food for fodder parasites?
lore.csrp.sim_cow: §lEpithet:§r Sim §l|§r §oStill reacts to the presence of feed and familiar sounds from husbandry, though only briefly. Once engaged, it lowers its head and drives forward with enough force to crush fencing or break bone. The contrast between its farm-bred mannerisms and sudden violence is deeply unsettling. It keeps wailing and crying whenever the sun rises. I don't know why.
lore.csrp.sim_cowhead: §lEpithet:§r Desim §l|§r §oA decapitated host animated by crawling sinew. It smells like stomach acid and beef. Will seek to reunite with any pile of meat to hijack.
lore.csrp.sim_dragone: §lEpithet:§r Sim §l|§r §oFlight appears difficult for its body, suggesting severe anatomical compromise. Even so, it remains highly lethal during descent and close approach. It seems to compensate for its failing body with distance and flight. Armor recovered from corpses often shows tearing and melted patterns, consistent with dipping tin foil in acid rather than clean predation. It does not seem acclimated to its body yet, as evidenced by it repeatedly thrashing its skull against the obsidian pillars of the End like a mace.
lore.csrp.sim_dragonehead: §lEpithet:§r Desim §l|§r §oAncient bone and teeth driven by fresh hunger. Still can use its rancid breath somehow.
lore.csrp.sim_enderman: §lEpithet:§r Sim §l|§r §oDisplays unstable teleportation behavior and little concern for its own condition. When set ablaze, it does not retreat as expected and may instead continue advancing, igniting anything nearby in the process. It shows no sign of preserving itself and will throw itself into water despite its seemingly toxic nature. This suggests pain response has either been dulled or rendered irrelevant. Its beheaded variant doesn't seem to be affected by water for some reason, though.
lore.csrp.sim_endermanhead: §lEpithet:§r Desim §l|§r §oStill looks... still finds. Still works. Still annoying. Can only carry the things of a similar size.
lore.csrp.sim_horse: §lEpithet:§r Sim §l|§r §oThe abdomen is swollen with pressurized putrid matter, making even minor trauma hazardous. It startles easily under force, heat, or sudden rupture and may detonate before full collapse. Despite this instability, it can still close distance quickly. I've seen it thrash and cry like a living horse moments before detonation.
lore.csrp.sim_horsehead: §lEpithet:§r Desim §l|§r §oGallops on rotten skin-covered tendrils where legs once were. Will seek to reunite with any pile of meat to hijack.
lore.csrp.sim_human: §lEpithet:§r Sim §l|§r §oRetains more recognizable behavior than most infected stock. Some specimens hesitate at doorways, look toward voices, or recoil from sudden heat before resuming attack. These reactions imply awareness has not been fully erased. They are difficult to study for long, as their movements often resemble panic as much as hostility. I can't discern what emotions they might be exhibiting.
lore.csrp.sim_humanhead: §lEpithet:§r Desim §l|§r §oIts hollow sockets hold enough shape to form a gaze. Will seek to reunite with any pile of meat to hijack.
lore.csrp.sim_pig: §lEpithet:§r Sim §l|§r §oAt a distance, it can still pass for an ordinary animal, especially when idle. Closer observation reveals constant chewing motions and abrupt changes in focus. It roots through organic waste, remains, and contaminated growth with equal interest. Very little of the original temperament appears intact, other than its impressive intelligence. I've seen it mindlessly roll around in the dirt and dig up carrots, but they just fall out of its maw, seemingly unwilling to commit to fully consuming them.
lore.csrp.sim_pighead: §lEpithet:§r Desim §l|§r §oSnuffling mass tethered by cords of meat. It still oinks. Will seek to reunite with any pile of meat to hijack.
lore.csrp.sim_sheep: §lEpithet:§r Sim §l|§r §oIts crying is among the worst sounds recorded from infected livestock. The vocalization resembles an ordinary bleat, but prolonged listening reveals a strained, wet quality unlike anything natural. Nearby specimens sometimes grow more active when it cries. Whether this is communication or simple agitation is still unknown. I've noticed they can be dyed in a few select colors. Why anyone would want to do that, I don't know.
lore.csrp.sim_sheephead: §lEpithet:§r Desim §l|§r §oWool matted with living threads. Will seek to reunite with any pile of meat to hijack.
lore.csrp.sim_squid: §lEpithet:§r Sim §l|§r §oMoves through water with an almost passive grace, shedding rot, debris, and infectious matter as it drifts. Areas it frequents become visibly fouled over time. It shows little urgency when approached. The surrounding current often carries pieces of it farther than the body travels. I can't tell which end is its mouth. Maybe it has two.
lore.csrp.sim_villager: §lEpithet:§r Sim §l|§r §oStill turns its head toward movement with the same curious rhythm seen in normal villagers. Some have been observed lingering near doors, workstations, and former gathering places. The resemblance ends the moment one closes distance. Whatever social instinct remains has been hollowed out and repurposed into a grotesque imitation. I've seen one that did not approach in open aggression, though it looked nothing like a villager. Six legs, long hair, and an odd 'face'. Something tall and pulsing runs along the back of its neck. I once watched it place something strange into the hands of another thing nearby, as though carrying out some sort of exchange. I feel like it's trying to say something, but I can't make sense of its hollow noises. Not yet, anyway.
lore.csrp.sim_villagerhead: §lEpithet:§r Desim §l|§r §oMutters in a voice that isn't language. Will seek to reunite with any pile of meat to hijack.
lore.csrp.sim_wolf: §lEpithet:§r Sim §l|§r §oResponds quickly to movement and rarely attacks without testing distance first. Multiple specimens will begin circling behavior even when no clear pack leader is present, implying the old instinct survives in broken form. Maybe it's chasing its own tail? Bites are fast, repetitive, and often aimed low, toward ankles. I've seen some with collars still strapped around their necks, and they react oddly when their former names, printed on their collars, are called out.
lore.csrp.sim_wolfhead: §lEpithet:§r Desim §l|§r §oThinking is optional. Will seek to reunite with any pile of meat to hijack.
lore.csrp.thrall: §lEpithet:§r Mes §l|§r §oObedience made flesh. Its body hangs together like a butchered thing forced back upright, with dark trailing filaments lashing behind it like severed reins. They are often found near places once crowded with life, kneading and worrying at the objects of vanished routine. The feet have warped into hard, hoof-like stumps, and the face has drawn into a melted expression too ruined to call human, yet still recognizably trying.
lore.csrp.vigilante: §lEpithet:§r Anged §l|§r §4WIP§o§0 §l|§r Hunts outliers and stragglers. It is a good job, mate.
lore.csrp.warden: §lEpithet:§r Ganro §l|§r §4WIP§o§0 §l|§r Bulwark organism. Holds its authority and ground like a tumor.
lore.csrp.worm: §lEpithet:§r Rof §l|§r §4WIP§o§0 §l|§r Coming into contact with such a creature is difficult. How did you manage that?
lore.csrp.wraith: §lEpithet:§r Elvia §l|§r §4WIP§o§0 §l|§r Half-anchored to flesh, half to nightmare; passes where walls do not. Fires a headache of a projectile.
